name: list_invoices
title: List invoices
description:
List and search invoices with optional filters for status, payment state, Person or Company, and more.

Supports filtering by invoice status (draft/issued/void), payment status, Person or Company, and archive state.
Returns invoice number, Person or Company name, total, balance due, status, and due date.
Payment states: `paid` is settled; `unpaid`, `overdue`, and `partial` are all subsets of money
still owed. Use payment_status="outstanding" to match ALL still-owed invoices at once (unpaid +
overdue + partial) — this is the usual intent of "outstanding"/"owed"/"unpaid". Use
payment_status="overdue" (with order_by="due_date") only for the narrower "what's past due?".
Responses include record ids; response_format='concise' returns trimmed rows (ids kept), 'detailed' adds links and secondary fields.
A returned page is capped at `limit` and is NOT necessarily the full matching set — the
header reads "Showing N of M" and calls out when more results exist. Pass
count_only=true for an EXACT total with no rows fetched (the right tool for "how many
invoices …?"); prefer get_entity_counts for a simple org-wide invoice count instead.

payment_status.title: Payment Status
payment_status.description: Filter by payment state. `paid` = settled. `unpaid`, `overdue`, and `partial` all mean money is still owed — `overdue` is simply an unpaid invoice past its due date. Use `outstanding` to match every still-owed invoice (unpaid + overdue + partial) in one call; use `overdue` only for the narrower 'what's past due?' question.

company_id.title: Company Id
company_id.description: Company UUID from list_companies or view_company; never substitute a Person UUID.

person_id.title: Person Id
person_id.description: Person UUID from list_people or view_person; never substitute a Company UUID.

response_format.title: Response Format
response_format.description: 'detailed' (default) matches today's full output, including links and secondary fields. 'concise' trims each row to essentials but always keeps '[id: ...]' for follow-up view/write tools.

count_only.title: Count Only
count_only.description: If true, return only the exact count of matching invoices, without fetching rows. Use this for 'how many invoices…?'.

name: create_invoice
title: Create invoice
description:
Create a draft invoice atomically with a new operation UUID and at least one line item.

Set command.party to {kind: person|company, id: UUID} from list_people/list_companies;
a draft may omit it until the recipient is known. No Company is created for a Person.
Use business_settings for currency/tax defaults and list_services for service IDs.
Omitted currency uses the business default; issue/due dates default to today/+30 days.
New line items must not carry retained IDs. Retry identical inputs with the same
operation UUID after an uncertain response; the same invoice is returned.

description.title: Description

quantity.description: Number of units. Omitted quantity is preserved on a retained item; new items default to one.
quantity.title: Quantity

unit_price.description: Price per unit; zero is valid.

discount_applied.description: Discount percent (0–100) or fixed amount, according to discount_type.
discount_applied.title: Discount Applied

sales_tax_applied.description: Tax rate as a decimal, such as 0.13.
sales_tax_applied.title: Sales Tax Applied

name: list_deals
title: List deals
description:
List pipeline deals.

Defaults to live, non-archived deals: approved deals assigned to a
pipeline stage. Set review_state to pending, dismissed, approved, or all
to inspect other review states. Use search for target name or company
text. Pass include_archived=True to also see archived (closed-out)
deals — omitted by default since an archived deal is something the
user explicitly removed from their board.
Responses include record ids; response_format='concise' returns trimmed rows (ids kept), 'detailed' adds links and secondary fields.
Renders an interactive pipeline board grouped by stage where supported.

response_format.title: Response Format
response_format.description: 'detailed' (default) matches today's full output, including links and secondary fields. 'concise' trims each row to essentials but always keeps '[id: ...]' for follow-up view/write tools.

name: get_pipeline_summary
title: Get pipeline summary
description:
Summarize active deal counts, linked value by stage, and pending-review count.

Renders an interactive pipeline board grouped by stage where supported.

name: move_deal_stage
title: Move deal stage
description:
Move a deal to Lead, Opportunity, Won, or Lost.

This is an operator/manual move and allows corrections such as moving out
of Won/Lost. Moving to Won requires the deal to already be linked to a
Person or Company; a missing target must be assigned before moving to Won.

name: send_invoice
title: Send invoice
description:
Call preview_document_send first and echo its recipients object unchanged. Approval binds this document and the displayed To/CC. Stale or changed recipients require a new preview.

Send an invoice to its checked recipients. Sets invoice status to 'issued'.

IMPORTANT: Only call this when the user explicitly asks to send/email the invoice.
Do NOT auto-send after creating — invoices are created as drafts for review first.
This sends a real email to the displayed To and CC email addresses.

digest.description: Digest returned by preview_document_send; echo unchanged.
digest.title: Digest

to.description: Exact To address shown by the preview and approval.
to.title: To

cc.description: Exact ordered CC addresses from the preview.
cc.title: Cc

name: ask_assistant
title: Ask assistant
description:
Read-only Q&A fallback. Use a specific tool first; reach for this only when no other tool fits.

PREFER specific tools whenever the request maps to one:
- Listing/filtering: list_invoices, list_people, list_companies, list_proposals, list_payments, list_expenses, list_services, list_deals, list_prospects, get_pipeline_summary
- Lookup by id/number/name: view_invoice, view_person, view_company, view_proposal, view_deal, view_prospect
- Read-only summaries: network_summary, get_daily_brief, get_heartbeat_summary, get_financial_report
- Mutations: create_invoice, create_proposal, create_person, create_company, record_payment, send_invoice, create_deal, move_deal_stage, log_deal_activity, etc.
- Capability/help: what_every_does for "what can Every do?", get_home for onboarding/welcome.

USE THIS TOOL ONLY for analytical questions that span multiple data points and have no
direct tool — e.g. "what's my revenue this quarter?", "which customers have the most
overdue invoices?", "summarize my pipeline this month". It is read-only: writes,
drafts, sends, deletes, and external MCP actions are refused. For changes, use the
specific write tools (create_invoice, record_payment, send_invoice, create_deal,
move_deal_stage, log_deal_activity, etc.).

Simple questions answer in seconds on a warm conversation; complex analytical
questions can take a minute or more, so keep first questions focused. Follow-up
questions asked within about 30 minutes reuse the same conversation thread, so you
can ask naturally without repeating earlier context.

message.title: Message
message.description: Fallback question for analysis that spans multiple data points (e.g. revenue, pipeline summaries, cross-entity rollups). Prefer specific tools — list_*, view_*, create_*, what_every_does, get_home — when one fits the request.

name: preview_document_send
title: Preview document send
description: Read the current recipient digest and exact To/CC for an invoice or proposal. Echo recipients unchanged into send_invoice/send_proposal so the approval names the intended recipients. Does not send anything or grant Portal access. Use the document ID from its list/view tool.

name: list_people
title: List People
description: Search People by name, email, phone or employer. Results include typed keys, avatars and profile versions. A Person may have multiple Companies or none. Page through has_more before treating results as complete.

name: list_companies
title: List Companies
description: Search Companies. A Company can exist without People. Results include typed keys, avatars and profile versions; private fields obey your billing role. Page through has_more before treating results as complete.
